data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact REDUCES TO SRC_005's core distinction: idempotency asks whether f(f(x)) = f(x) when the second f receives the original x, while safety asks whether applying f again after it has already mutated state to f(x) causes harm. The isolated artifact's treatment of writer safety for append-only logs reduces to this single distinction because the 'harm' in question is duplicate entries corrupting deterministic replay, and the 'original state' vs 'mutated state' difference is exactly what makes appending non-idempotent but potentially safe. Every engineering prescription in the neighbourhood follows from applying this one conceptual fork to the concrete case of append-only event logs under at-least-once delivery. REFUTED IF the isolated artifact invokes additional conceptual machinery beyond the original-state-vs-mutated-state distinction—for example, if it requires notions of causality, partial ordering, or consensus that are not derivable from SRC_005's formulation alone, showing the reduction is incomplete.
